name: Hurricane #1
label: Creation Records
lede: Andy Bell wrote the songs after Ride, Alex Lowe sang them, and Creation got two albums before Bell left to play bass in Oasis. Fifteen years later, Alan McGee talked Lowe into bringing it back.

eras.title: Bell writes, Lowe sings
eras.text: With Ride finished, Andy Bell stayed at Creation Records and built a band around a singer for his songs. The first year brought a top 20 hit, a top 20 album and slots on Top of the Pops, TFI Friday, T in the Park and Glastonbury.

years.src: Penny Black Music: Ride · Creation Records: Hurricane#1 · Wikipedia: Andy Bell · Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1 · Louder Than War: Interview: Alex Lowe · Louder Than War: Hurricane#1: New Album
years.h: Andy Bell starts a band in Oxford and gives the mic to Alex Lowe
years.p: Bell plays lead guitar and writes; Lowe sings and plays guitar, with Will Pepper on bass and Gareth 'Gaz' Farmer on drums. Creation signs them.
years.xp:
Bell didn't hide the model. Wikipedia quotes him saying the band was "inspired by Oasis," Creation's biggest act. "It really was Alan that encouraged me to get the new band together," he told Penny Black Music in 1997, placing the sound "somewhere between Stone Roses and Oasis."

Lowe auditioned in May 1996 at Sanctuary Studios in London, "well nervous but confident." He was a former amateur boxer with about 35 fights behind him, and gives the credit for his break to two people: "if it wasn't for Alan McGee and Andy Bell I wouldn't be talking to you."

The band started out as Hurricane and added the #1 rather than argue over the name with DJ Hurricane.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1 · Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1 (album) · Creation Records: Hurricane#1
yt: 'Step into My World' on TFI Friday, May 1997
years.h: 'Step into My World' reaches No. 29, then a remix makes No. 19
years.p: The debut single charts on its own; [[Paul Oakenfold|7bf1f441-ccf1-4258-9797-07c8d16eb44c]]'s remix later in 1997 does better.
years.xp: Nobody in the band saw it coming. "We thought it would end up going to 60 in the charts," Lowe said in 2001.

years.h: The debut, made in Lincoln, goes to No. 11
years.p: Bell and Stephen Harris produce at Chapel Studio. 'Just Another Illusion' and 'Chain Reaction' come out as singles around it; Wikipedia puts sales at 100,000.
years.xp: Reviews split. NME gave it 5 out of 10 and The Observer heard "ponderously paced retro-rock." Q listed it among the year's best, and The Guardian liked its "quality-crafted trad rock."

eras.title: Drum machines, then Oasis
eras.text: The second album went electronic, with samples and programming, and its title track matched the band's best chart placing. By the end of 1999 Bell was in Oasis and Hurricane #1 was over.

years.src: Wikipedia: Only the Strongest Will Survive · Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1 · Creation Records: Hurricane#1
yt: On Top of the Pops, February 1998
years.h: 'Only the Strongest Will Survive' gets to No. 19
years.p: The title track of the second album comes out more than a year ahead of the record. 'Rising Sign' follows in October.
years.xp: During the Creation years The Sun used one of Bell's Hurricane #1 songs in an advert, and the music press, the NME above all, called it selling out. Lowe, in 2001: "You don't have to buy the Sun to like the song."

years.src: Wikipedia: Only the Strongest Will Survive · Louder Than War: Interview: Alex Lowe
years.h: Steve Sidelnyck programs, Ian McLagan plays keys
years.p: The second album runs 75 minutes and leans on drum machines and sampling. It stops at No. 55 in the UK and makes the top 20 in Japan.
years.xp: Bell wrote everything except 'What Do I Know?', which is Lowe's. "I wrote three or four for B-sides," Lowe told Louder Than War, and one for this record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Andy Bell · Louder Than War: Hurricane#1: New Album · Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1 · Creation Records: Hurricane#1
years.h: Bell moves to Sweden, then gets the call from Oasis
years.p: With Hurricane #1 on hold, Bell relocates with his family and is asked to join [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]] on bass, an instrument he has to learn. The band ends.
years.xp:
Lowe has said Bell had writer's block at the end, and that Creation was in the middle of selling up to Sony. Lowe also says Bell played with [[Gay Dad|c2cd7d06-4236-470b-badf-f3a52a3992c4]] before Oasis; Wikipedia says the Gay Dad report was false.

Lowe and Liam Gallagher had fallen out the first time they met, at Ronnie Scott's. Lowe says Liam took his Scottish way of saying hello personally.

eras.title: Lowe on his own
eras.text: Without Bell, Lowe drifted from music into painting and smaller bands. Then cancer, and a call from Alan McGee.

years.h: Step into My World collects the band in 2004
years.p: A compilation keeps the Creation-era songs in print.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1 · Louder Than War: Hurricane#1: New Album
years.h: Lowe forms Garage Flowers, and starts painting
years.p: Gun Club Cemetery follows in 2013. "I got sick of the industry at one point," Lowe told Louder Than War.
years.xp: "Painting gave me a new lease of life, it made me see the world in a whole different way," he said.

q: Alex, reform Hurricane #1, the time is right for this!
years.src: Louder Than War: Interview: Alex Lowe · Louder Than War: Hurricane#1: New Album · Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1
years.h: Alan McGee tells Lowe to bring the band back
years.p: Lowe is in treatment for cancer when McGee calls. In November a new line-up is announced: Lowe, the Mariani brothers and drummer Chris Campbell.
years.xp: Lowe told Louder Than War he went through chemotherapy, radiotherapy, blood transfusions and kidney dialysis. "I should be dead but here I am," he said in 2017.

eras.title: Back on Tapete
eras.text: The new Hurricane #1 is Lowe's band, writing his own songs, mostly for the German label Tapete Records. The line-up changed around him, with The Seahorses' Stuart Fletcher arriving on bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1 · Louder Than War: Interview: Alex Lowe
years.h: Lowe writes the comeback album during his treatment
years.p: He meant Find What You Love and Let It Kill You to be uplifting, not sad. Of fifteen songs he wrote, twelve made the record.

years.src: Louder Than War: Hurricane #1: Stereo, Glasgow
years.h: Lowe back on stage at Stereo in Glasgow
years.p: The second-to-last night of the reunion's UK tour, months after dialysis and chemotherapy.

years.src: Louder Than War: Hurricane#1: New Album · Say It With Garage Flowers · Wikipedia: Hurricane No. 1
years.h: Melodic Rainbows comes out in Japan first
years.p: Strawberry Moon Records puts it out, with the UK release following in October 2017. "The band is now a band," Lowe said.
years.xp: Lowe told Sean Hannam he was after "a guitar album full of noise." He still thought the first band "should never have split up."

years.h: Stuart Fletcher of the Seahorses takes the bass
years.p: Jon Roberts replaces Carlo Mariani on guitar the next year, in time for Buddah at the Gas Pump (2019).

years.h: Backstage Waiting to Go On is the fourth reunion album
years.p: Released on Tapete, like Find What You Love and Let It Kill You and Buddah at the Gas Pump before it.
